lead: Large blocks in a steeply sloping valley, at the foot of Collserola.
text: It was built from 1963 in an area where a cemetery had been planned, on the land of the old Vallbona stables, and it was born without urban services or basic facilities. It lies in a steeply sloping valley on the hill of les Roquetes, and its construction had a major impact on the Collserola range. In 2024 an amendment to the general plan covering 33,642 m² was provisionally approved to improve sports facilities, with a new municipal sports centre in Can Cuiàs, and the connection with Collserola; final approval is still pending. The Pla de Barris 2025-2028 also provides for 7 million euros to renovate the five public schools of the northern part of Nou Barris (Zona Nord).

Some of its shortcomings have been addressed with metro line 11, a light metro whose Ciutat Meridiana station is its main connection. With 11,493 inhabitants in 0.38 km², the density is 30,485 inhabitants/km², and the neighbourhood is still made up of large residential blocks. At 2,660 €/m² and 601 €/month, it is among the most affordable in Barcelona. If you are selling, the average sale price is 10% below the Nou Barris average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 213,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Nou Barris (7th of 13 by price). If you are investing, the average rent is 24% below the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Large residential blocks in a steeply sloping valley.
